title: Trace, Determinant and Inverse of a Matrix
breadcrumb: Mathematics → Matrix algebra → Trace, determinant and inverse
objectives: Compute trace and use its linear, cyclic and similarity properties.
Apply determinant rules for products, transposes, scalar multiples and inverses.
Decide invertibility using determinant and rank.
Compute 2×2 and general inverses using adjugates.
Apply inverse product and transpose identities.

prereq.name: Matrix addition and multiplication
prereq.why: Trace and product identities rely on matrix operations.

prereq.name: Determinants and cofactors
prereq.why: The inverse formula uses determinant and adjugate.

prereq.name: Eigenvalues
prereq.why: Trace and determinant are the sum and product of eigenvalues.

traps: Trace cyclicity allows cyclic permutations, not arbitrary rearrangement of factors.
det(cA)=cⁿdet(A) for n×n A; it is not c det(A) unless n=1.
A singular matrix has no inverse; do not divide by zero determinant.
The adjugate is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.

sheet: A invertible iff det(A)≠0 iff rank(A)=n.
tricks: For trace(AB), compute only diagonal entries if multiplying directly.
Use det(AB) multiplicativity rather than expanding a large determinant.
Remember the power n in det(cA).
Reverse factor order when inverting a product.
Check det(A) before using the adjugate formula.
shortcuts: Similar matrices have equal trace and determinant.
remember: Inverse of a product reverses order.

howto: Memorise the product and scalar rules, then practise the inverse formula on 2×2 matrices. For multi-step identities, track dimensions and order carefully. Trace cyclicity is not full commutativity.

scenes.title: Matrix quantities and dimensions
scenes.objective: Recall trace, determinant and inverse conditions.

ask.q: What condition makes a square matrix invertible?

body: For a square matrix A, the trace is the sum of diagonal entries. The determinant measures signed volume scaling and detects singularity.
A is invertible exactly when det(A) is non-zero. The inverse satisfies AA⁻¹=A⁻¹A=I. Trace is defined for every square matrix; determinant and inverse are also square-matrix concepts.
This lesson connects the computational rules with the structural identities that commonly appear in NET-JRF questions.

scenes.title: Trace: definition and identities
scenes.objective: Use linearity and cyclic trace identities.

blocks.body: tr(A)=Σᵢ aᵢᵢ. For compatible square products, tr(A+B)=tr(A)+tr(B), tr(cA)=c tr(A), and tr(AB)=tr(BA).
For compatible rectangular A and B, tr(AB)=tr(BA) whenever both products are square. For three factors, tr(ABC)=tr(BCA)=tr(CAB), but arbitrary reordering is not permitted.
In general AB≠BA. Trace equality does not mean the matrices themselves are equal. Trace is also similarity-invariant: tr(P⁻¹AP)=tr(A).

ask.nudge: A scalar equality is much weaker than equality of matrices.

scenes.title: Worked trace calculation
scenes.objective: Calculate traces without multiplying unnecessary entries.

ask.nudge: Compute the diagonal entries of AB.

steps.why: Only the diagonal entries contribute to trace.
The matrices differ, but their traces agree.

scenes.title: Determinant: core properties
scenes.objective: Use determinant rules to simplify products and transformations.

blocks.body: For n×n A, det(cA)=cⁿdet(A). Swapping two rows changes sign; multiplying one row by c multiplies the determinant by c; adding a multiple of one row to another leaves it unchanged.
det(A)=0 iff rows or columns are linearly dependent iff A is singular iff A⁻¹ does not exist.

scenes.title: Determinants and powers
scenes.objective: Apply product identities to powers and inverses.

steps.why: The inverse determinant is the reciprocal.

blocks.body: The order reverses because (AB)(B⁻¹A⁻¹)=A(BB⁻¹)A⁻¹=I. Do not write A⁻¹B⁻¹.

ask.q: What is the inverse of AB?
ask.nudge: Reverse the order and invert each factor.

scenes.title: The 2×2 inverse formula
scenes.objective: Compute an inverse using the adjugate.

steps.why: The determinant is non-zero, so the inverse exists.
Swap diagonal entries and change signs of off-diagonal entries.

scenes.title: Adjugate and general inverse
scenes.objective: State and apply the adjugate formula.

blocks.body: For nonsingular square A, A⁻¹=adj(A)/det(A), where adj(A) is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.
The cofactor Cᵢⱼ=(−1)ⁱ⁺ʲMᵢⱼ, where Mᵢⱼ is the minor after deleting row i and column j. The adjugate is Cᵀ.
Multiply A by the proposed inverse. The product must be I. For numerical questions, also check det(A)≠0 before applying the formula.

ask.q: For a nonsingular matrix, what is A adj(A)?
ask.nudge: It is a scalar multiple of the identity.

blocks.body: The trace equals the sum of eigenvalues and determinant equals their product, both counted with algebraic multiplicity.
Similar matrices have the same characteristic polynomial, trace, determinant and eigenvalues. If B=P⁻¹AP, then det(B)=det(A) and tr(B)=tr(A).

ask.q: A 2×2 matrix has eigenvalues 2 and −3. Find its trace and determinant.

scenes.title: One-page matrix identity sheet
scenes.objective: Retain the formulas that save time in the exam.
body: Trace: tr(A+B)=tr(A)+tr(B), tr(cA)=c tr(A), tr(AB)=tr(BA), and trace is similarity-invariant.
Invertibility: det(A)≠0 iff A⁻¹ exists. Adjugate formula: A⁻¹=adj(A)/det(A).
